description: Rick crosses Britain to ask what the country actually eats now, pairing farms, fisheries and old regional dishes with immigrant kitchens, modern producers and the people who have quietly expanded the definition of British food.

s14e01.description: In Cumbria, Rick cooks mutton hotpot with farmer and writer James Rebanks, follows Morecambe Bay shrimp and revisits shepherd's pie with his son Jack, linking familiar dishes to the farms and estuary that sustain them.

s14e02.description: Argyll brings Pamela Brunton's local and foraged cooking, langoustines, a traditional smokehouse and tattie scones, showing how the west-coast landscape keeps seafood and preserved food at the centre of everyday meals.

s14e03.description: Rick visits James Dyson's farm to see robotic strawberry production, then explores Lincolnshire plum bread and sausages before making strawberry sorbet and a particularly local version of bangers and mash.

s14e04.description: A Filipino Sunday lunch, a chef committed to using the whole fish and dry-aged local beef reveal a changing Northern Irish food culture, while Rick cooks adobo and a beef-and-Guinness pie.

s14e05.description: Bury Market and north-west food traditions lead to chef Joe Otway and Manchester's music history, while Rick moves from a Scotch-egg ploughman's lunch to old-school liver, bacon and onions.

s14e06.description: Salt-marsh lamb and the unexploded remnants of wartime bombing share a landscape with rhubarb pizza and traditional coracle fishing, ending with smoked sea trout pulled from Welsh waters.

s14e07.description: Bristol's Caribbean community and carnival lead Rick to jerk chicken, while a café staffed by survivors of trafficking and the city's enthusiasm for fermentation broaden the story before a generous burrito.

s14e08.description: Artisan sourdough, a beach fish seller and George Orwell's writing on English food frame Suffolk, where Rick adds Japanese technique with sushi and maki rather than pretending British food developed in isolation.

s14e09.description: Rick treats London as a city of more than a hundred cuisines, moving through Chinatown dim sum and mozzarella making before discussing the full English with Stuart Maconie and cooking chow mein with peaches.

s14e10.description: A Ukrainian community kitchen and borscht lead to brewer Jaega Wise and Walthamstow's film history, while Rick cooks chicken Kyiv and John Dory with beer, bacon and lettuce.

s14e11.description: Kent's cherries and Dover sole take Rick from orchards to Margate, where Turner's coast and the culture of fish and chips meet sole meunière and a batch of cherry cupcakes.

s14e12.description: Glasgow's Korean, Pakistani and Italian communities share the episode with an artisan chocolatier, giving Rick room for both profiteroles and osso buco while tracing how migration remade the city's food.

s14e13.description: Yorkshire pudding history sits beside Indian-style mushy peas, local bitter and a tofu factory, before Rick moves between tofu pad Thai and paneer jalfrezi to test what 'Yorkshire food' now means.

s14e14.description: Leicester's Indian food with Gurdeep Loyal, Birmingham chef Aktar Islam and a chapati-flour mill trace the Midlands' South Asian culinary life, culminating in a look at Britain's peculiar relationship with chicken tikka masala.

s14e15.description: Organic farming pioneer Guy Singh-Watson, cheesemaker Mary Quicke and chef Mark Hix give the West Country finale its producers, while Rick cooks carrot tarte tatin and a savoury filo pie.
